lawyer:
H.K. Abdul Hye with S.K. Ashraf Hossain ----- For the appellant.
A.F.M. Shahid ----- For the State.
parties:
Abdul Hafez Sardar ----- Appellant.
Vs.
The State ----- Respondent.
full_judgment:
On 22-7-68 appellant Abdul Hafez Sardar along with another Abdul Sattar Khan was convicted by the Sessions Judge and Ex-Officio Special Judge, Comilla. The appellant Abdul Hafez Sardar was convicted under section 409 /109 P.C. and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7 days land to pay a fine of Rs. 1000/- in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2 months and the other accused Abdul Sat tar Khan was convicted under section 409/109 P.C., and sentenced to imprisonment till rising of the Court and to pay a fine of Rs. 100/-, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 1 month. He, however, acquitted accused Abdul Hafez Sardar of the charge under section 467 P.C. and the other accused Abdul Sattar Khan under section 467/109 P.C. accused Abdul Sattar Khan has not appealed. 

 2. The prosecution case is that appellant Abdul Hafez Sardar was a member of union No. 6 Tarapurchandi, P.S. Chandpur, District Comilla. The appellant as the Chairman of the Project Committee received As. 405/- from Abdul Hakim, Chairman of the Union Committee on 22-9-66 for the year 1965-66 for the repair and reconstruction of two bridges within the union council. The other accused Abdul Sattar Khan was a member of the Project Committee. The work was executed by these two persons. It is said that they prepared 3 false vouchers of Rs. 44/- Rs. 22.50 paisa and Rs. 87.88 paisa in total Rs. 154.38 paisa in the name of 3 fictitious persons namely Afazuddin Jamadar, Nur Mohammad and Fajarali. They were therefore charged with misappropriation by creating fake and forged vouchers 

 6. The prosecution has examined P.W.1 Abdul Majid Bandukshi who was the first complainant regarding the alleged misappropriation. All he has said is that a sum of Rs. 80/90/- was spent and that there was no person in their union in the names of Kajimuddin Chowkidar, Nur Mohammad, Afajuddin and Fajarali. P.W. 5 Moulana Abdul Hakim is the Chairman of the Union Council. He has proved that an amount of Rs. 405/- for the repair and reconstruction of bridges was given to Abdul Hafez Sarder, the member and Ex-Officio Chairman of the Ward Committee No. 6. He has also proved the Advance and Adjustment Register, Ext. 8 and the cash-book, Ext. 9. He has proved the signature of the accused. He stated that he did not receive any complaint regarding the work on the two bridges. In his cross-examination he admitted that Ext. A, the resolution was submitted to him by the accused. He also admitted that there was no expert opinion as to the amount spent on the two bridges. He further admitted that on the objection of the accused, he called Afazuddin and got the vouchers signed. P.W.9 Abdul Samad Bandukshi is another witness examined by the prosecution who said that he could not say if there was any person named Kajimuddin Chowkidar in village Dashandi, and he opined that a sum of Rs. 80-90/- might have been spent on the two bridges. The Investigation Officer P.W. 13 also opined that a sum of Rs. 80/90/- might have been spent on the two bridges. The prosecution has examined P.W. 8 Afajuddin Jamadar himself who said that he did not sign any Muster Roll, and that he got Rs. 8/- only and according to his opinion a sum of Rs. 115/120/- might have been spent on account of the repair of one of the bridges near the school. He did not see the other bridge, The prosecution has tried to rely mainly on the evidence of the hand writing expert P.W. 2 to whom some vouchers, Advance and Adjustment Register, two Muster Rolls and the specimen writings of the two accused persons and Afajuddin Jamadar were sent. Though he opined that the writing in the Advance and Adjustment Register and the Muster Rolls are in the handwriting of the two accused, still he could not say that the names of Nur Mohammad, Fazar Ali or Afajuddin Jamadar were forged. The evidences of the other witnesses are more or less in the formal nature, and need not be discussed. The trial Judge came to the finding that from the evidence of P.W. 2 handwriting expert no forgery was committed in respect of the signatures of Nut Mohammad, Kazimuddin, Fazar All or Afajuddin. He also found that the plea of accused Abdul Hafez Sarder that he handed over the entire money to Abdus Sattar Khan by virtue of Ext. C could not be relied upon and therefore both of them were responsible for the work. He also disbelieved the evidence of P. W. 8 Afajuddin and found that Afajuddin signed the Muster Roll. Therefore, he came to the conclusion that prosecution has failed to establish the case of forgery and the abetment of it against both the accused persons. The reasons are worth acceptance. 

 11. The above finding shows that the prosecution case as a whole has failed, but the other accused Abdus Sattar Khan has not appealed and the question is what can be done with regard to his conviction and sentence under section 409/109 P.C. Both the learned Advocates have cited three decisions before me. They are 2 D.L.R. pages 304; P.L.D. 1949 Lahore, page 179; and P.L.D. 1965 Karachi, page 637. A reading of the said decisions shows that the High Court can under section 439 Cr.P.C. suo motu take cognizance of the case of an accused that has not appealed, and set aside his conviction and sentence. I am in respectful agreement with the aforesaid decisions. 1, therefore, suo motu take cognizance of the case of Abdus Sattar Khan under section 439 Cr.P.C. I have already found that the prosecution case as a whole has failed and in this view of the matter the order of conviction and sentence of accused Abdus Sattar Khan under section 409/109 P.C. is quashed.
